content:
iPhone 18 Pro is about to be released, and with major changes to this year's product lineup, it's set to become the most prominent new iPhone in Apple's history.

Since there won't be a standard iPhone 18 this year, the iPhone 18 Pro will become Apple's default flagship new device.

For years, Apple has launched multiple new iPhones every year, and without a doubt, that will continue for many years to come.

But at Apple's event this week, the iPhone lineup will undergo significant changes.

Apple won't be offering the usual choice between the standard 'iPhone' and 'iPhone Pro'—the standard iPhone 18 will be absent.

Multiple sources indicate that Apple will delay the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 until early 2027, so the fall lineup will only include:

With the iPhone 18 pushed beyond the traditional release cycle, the iPhone 18 Pro essentially becomes Apple's new default model.

Users looking for more affordable options can still choose the iPhone 17, iPhone 17e, or iPhone Air released last year. However, with no 'iPhone 18' to promote as the new flagship this fall and holiday season, Apple and its carrier partners will instead turn to the iPhone 18 Pro to fill that role.

The iPhone Ultra is priced too high, so its market position is likely to remain quite niche.

So for the average consumer wanting to buy 'the latest iPhone,' Apple will essentially offer only two choices: the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

This is an interesting experiment and could make the iPhone 18 Pro the best-selling Pro model of the new generation; but combined with expected price hikes, there's also risk for Apple. With no upgradable iPhone 18 available, users looking to upgrade may hold onto their existing iPhones for longer.

Regardless of the outcome, whether Apple's new arrangement works will be revealed soon.

What do you think of Apple's iPhone lineup changes this year? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
